To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the relationship between social engagement of users and customer profitability in the analyzed online customer network is not as simple and linear as it is often assumed.
“buyers” are not more socially active than “nonbuyers” in our sample of an online customer network of a German direct bank.
the relationship between social engagement and customer profit is not significant and that the effect of social engagement on customer profitability varies across different customer types.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how social engagement of customers in online customer networks is related to customer profitability.
the question whether the assumption of a positive relationship between social engagement and customer value holds true in practice.
the question of whether social engagement is really an indicator of future profitability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
social engagement is neither an indicator of future customer profitability nor of a higher likelihood for a customer to buy a product or service.
there is no generalizable relationship between customers’ social engagement and their profitability.
social engagement is not generally associated with higher customer profitability in online communities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
social engagement in online customer networks does not automatically lead to a better financial performance of the hosting company.
the social engagement of customers in online customer networks is a valuable source for companies, but it does not necessarily lead to a higher customer profitability.
the social engagement of customers in online customer networks is not a significant driver of customer profitability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
social engagement in online customer networks is not always a good predictor for customer profitability.
companies should be careful with generalizing the results from one company to others and that the relationship between social engagement and customer value is highly context-dependent.
the relationship between social engagement and customer profit is not as straightforward as it is often assumed.
